# Security policy

## Supported version

Fixes go onto the default branch and the deployed app. Older commits, forks,
and private deployments aren't maintained.

## Report a vulnerability privately

Don't put vulnerability details in a public issue, discussion, or PR.

Prefer [GitHub Private Vulnerability Reporting](https://github.com/w04m1/elte-schedule-builder/security/advisories/new).
Otherwise email `w04m1@proton.me`, subject `ELTE Schedule Builder security
report`.

Include:

- affected page, endpoint, or commit;
- reproduction steps or a minimal proof of concept;
- expected impact;
- whether it affects the deployed site, local installs, or both;
- a suggested fix, if you have one.

Strip personal data, credentials, and real student schedules — use `DEMO-*`
subjects when they reproduce the problem.

## What to expect

Acknowledgement within about seven days, then scope confirmation and a
coordinated fix and disclosure. Complex reports take longer. Please allow a
reasonable fix window before publishing.

## Scope and safe testing

Good-faith testing of this project's own code and deployment is welcome when
it avoids privacy violations, disruption, and destructive actions. Don't
target ELTE, Tanrend, Google, Imgur, hosting providers, or other third
parties. No DoS testing, no accessing other people's data.
